title: SSE resume granularity and function-call reconciliation shim
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
We need a pragmatic SSE resume strategy that balances resume granularity (byte/fragment/message/application) with deterministic function-call and structured-output reconciliation across reconnects. The goal is a compatibility shim that lets existing clients (JSONL + function-call framing) continue working while enabling finer-grained, safe resumes for new clients without breaking tool-calling semantics.

Goals:
- Provide a resume token format and server semantics that guarantee resumed streams do not re-deliver half-emitted structured outputs or partial function-call payloads to clients that expect atomic tool calls.
- Offer an opt-in higher-resolution resume mode for low-latency clients that tolerate reassembly (prefix merges) to reduce repeated tokens sent after reconnects.
- Maintain backward compatibility: legacy clients should see identical event boundaries as before.
- Expose negotiation headers so clients choose resume strategy per-connection.

Acceptance criteria:
- New SSE events contain stable metadata (event-id, seq, resume_token, boundary_type) emitted by runtime for each logical emission.
- Resume token can be used to resume from the last confirmed *application* boundary (safe default) or an optionally requested finer-grain point (fragment-level) with explicit client acknowledgement of potential duplicate/merge behavior.
- Function-call frames are never split across resume boundary in the safe/default mode.
- Unit + integration tests validate resume from: mid-token, mid-json-object, after function-call, and after streaming JSONL.
- Production rollout with canary (5% traffic) and dashboards for duplicate-message rate, tool-call replays, and resume success rate.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
1) Granularity levels:
   - application (default): resume only at top-level logical outputs (e.g., complete assistant messages or completed function-call objects). Guarantees idempotent replay semantics for most clients. Higher re-transmission cost on reconnect.
   - fragment: resume at more frequent micro-checkpoints (e.g., after each SSE chunk event). Lower retransmission overhead, but requires client reassembly and de-duplication. Provided as opt-in and only for clients that set X-Resume-Granularity: fragment.
   - byte-offset: considered but rejected for now due to large surface area and brittle semantics across intermediate transformations (compression, intermediate gateways).

2) Token format:
   - opaque base64 JSON payload signed by runtime key: {v, seq, last_app_boundary_seq, checksum, issued_at}. Server validates token and maps to persisted checkpoint (in-memory LRU + durable store for long-lived sessions).
   - token includes semantic pointer to last application boundary so safe resumes are trivial for servers.

3) Function-call reconciliation:
   - In application mode, server guarantees that a resume token never points into a function-call payload. Function-call events are emitted atomically with envelope metadata (tool_name, call_id, status: started|completed). The completed event is the application boundary.
   - For fragment mode, server still emits 'function-call-checkpoint' markers but attaches 'fragment_repair_hint' so clients can reconcile duplicates or merged fragments. Documentation will describe deterministic merge: favor longest suffix match + call_id dedupe.

4) Backoff and retry policy:
   - Clients should use exponential jittered backoff and send the last seen resume_token in a Resume-Token header. Server responds 200 and continues if token is valid, or 409 with earliest safe_resume_seq when token expired/invalid.

Implementation plan (high level):
- runtime: Emit event metadata on every SSE event: id (uuid), seq (monotonic int per-session), resume_token (for next safe boundary), boundary_type (application|fragment).
- protocol shim: Add negotiation headers: X-Resume-Granularity (application|fragment), X-Resume-Version. Default behavior unchanged if headers absent.
- persistence: small checkpoint store (LRU) keyed by session id -> last N seqs + token mapping. Long-lived sessions push token to durable store.
- compatibility shim: For clients requesting legacy JSONL/function-call behavior, runtime will synthesize legacy boundaries (legacy_event_marker) so downstream parsers and proxies see previous framing.

Testing & QA:
- Unit tests for token encoding/decoding, expiry and mapping to safe boundary.
- Integration tests simulating reconnects at: inside JSON object, inside function-call args, right after function-call completion. Validate no duplicate function-call completions in application mode.
- Chaos test harness to randomly drop connections and validate client-visible invariants.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge feature flag behind runtime config (streaming_resume_v2).
2) Canary: route 5% of streaming connections in us-west to new runtime. Monitor duplicate-tool-call rate, resume-failure rate, latency.
3) Gradual ramp to 100% with rollback policy if duplicate-tool-call rate increases >0.1% or resume-failure rate >1%.

Observability & dashboards:
- New metrics: resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, resume_conflicts(409), duplicate_function_call_count, avg_retransmit_tokens_per_resume.
- Tracing: annotate spans with seq/resume_token to correlate reconnect flow.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SSE+Resume+Granularity+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2148
- Client SDK notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/412

Notes:
- We intentionally avoid exposing internal checkpoint IDs to clients; tokens are opaque and signed.
- This design defers full byte-offset resume until we have stronger guarantees around intermediary modifications in the pipeline (compressors, proxies).
- Security review is not required for initial rollout but will be triggered if token lifetime extends beyond 24h.
